verifiedScope.proxy: Lifetime detective-novel first-book-publication span, from The Mysterious Affair at Styles to Curtain, used as a publishing proxy rather than a claim of uninterrupted writing. Markers use the earliest English-language book edition, not composition, periodical serialization, translation or adaptation dates. Styles appeared in the US in 1920 before its 1921 British book. And Then There Were None is shown under its current title with its original 1939 publication year. Curtain was written during World War II but held back until 1975; it was not her last novel composed. Sleeping Murder appeared posthumously in 1976 and does not extend the bar. Short stories, plays, poetry, nonfiction and the Mary Westmacott novels are outside this detective-novel scope.
